The Long Enlightenment by Robert Clancy
Significant Contributors
The Long Enlightenment: Australian Science from its Beginning to the Mid-20th Century
by Robert Clancy
Halstead Press, 2021, 184 pages, $49.95
Emeritus Professor Robert Clancy’s book The Long Enlightenment is a corrective to outmoded historical views on science in colonial and post-federation Australia. In 1964, the American historian Donald Flemming offhandedly asserted that the colonial scientist in the antipodes saw natural history as “the ideal refuge from the perilous enterprise of embarking upon theoretical constructs by which he would be pitched into naked competition with the best scholars”. In their book Australian Science in the Making (1988) Ian Inkster and Jan Todd summed up scientific activity before the Second World War as “utilitarian and localised” with a “pragmatic empirical emphasis”.
